chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who fell ill in the month of Ramadan, and when he recovered wished to perform Hajj, what should he do regarding the making up of the fast?
He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he returns, let him make it up.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever is obliged to make up the month of Ramadan or something of the obligatory fasting, it is not permissible for him to perform voluntary fasting until he fulfills what is obligatory upon him. This is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.قَضَاءُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Making up the month of Ramadan (fasts)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing voluntary fasting before making up missed obligatory fasts from Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the sequence of obligations for a pilgrim who missed Ramadan fasts due to illness, establishing that making up the fasts (Qada) takes precedence over voluntary acts. The Sheikh’s addition highlights a key jurisprudential principle: obligatory debts must be settled before engaging in supererogatory worship, ensuring the validity of both. This reflects the Shia emphasis on prioritizing definitive duties (Fard) over optional ones (Nafl) to maintain spiritual integrity.
